subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Endometrial Sampling

steps.tx: **Endometrial sampling** is a vital diagnostic procedure used to evaluate the uterine cavity for hyperplasia and endometrial adenocarcinoma in women presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding. The primary clinical indication is any episode of postmenopausal bleeding, where cancer risk reaches ten percent. In premenopausal women, sampling is mandatory in all patients aged forty-five and older, as well as those under forty-five with risk factors for unopposed estrogen exposure, including chronic anovulation, obesity with BMI over thirty, or Lynch syndrome.
steps.say: Endometrial biopsy rules out cancer in women with abnormal bleeding. It is mandatory for any postmenopausal bleeding, in all women aged forty-five and older with abnormal bleeding, and in younger women with obesity or PCOS.

vis.caption: Flexible Pipelle endometrial suction curette for office-based histopathological sampling. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Transvaginal ultrasonography** serves as the initial, non-invasive triage investigation for postmenopausal bleeding, measuring double-layer endometrial thickness in the mid-sagittal plane. In postmenopausal women not using hormone replacement therapy, an endometrial thickness of four millimetres or less carries a negative predictive value exceeding ninety-nine percent for endometrial cancer, permitting safe clinical observation. If the endometrial echo measures greater than four millimetres, or appears heterogeneous, irregular, or poorly visualized, immediate tissue histological sampling is mandatory.
steps.say: Transvaginal ultrasound measures endometrial thickness in postmenopausal bleeding. A measurement of four millimetres or less virtually excludes endometrial cancer, whereas thickness over four millimetres demands an immediate biopsy.

vis.title: Endometrial Thickness Thresholds in Postmenopausal Bleeding

steps.tx: **Pipelle suction curettage** is the current standard of care for outpatient office-based endometrial biopsy, replacing formal inpatient curettage under general anaesthesia. The instrument consists of a flexible 3.1 millimetre polypropylene sheath containing an internal plunger. After sterile bivalve speculum insertion, the Pipelle is gently advanced through the cervical os to the uterine fundus. Withdrawing the internal plunger creates negative suction, and the curette is rotated three hundred and sixty degrees while being drawn back to capture tissue strips.
steps.say: The Pipelle is an outpatient plastic curette that works through suction. Once inserted to the fundus, the piston is pulled back to create a vacuum, and the sheath is rotated three-sixty degrees to harvest tissue strips.

steps.tx: **Diagnostic accuracy** of the Pipelle biopsy exceeds ninety-nine percent for detecting global, diffuse endometrial adenocarcinoma in postmenopausal women. However, because blind Pipelle sampling samples approximately four to five percent of the internal endometrial surface area, its sensitivity falls significantly to sixty percent for localized focal lesions such as small polyps or focal malignancy. When blind sampling yields insufficient tissue, or when abnormal postmenopausal bleeding persists despite a benign biopsy result, definitive diagnostic hysteroscopy is urgently required.
steps.say: Pipelle biopsy detects over ninety-nine percent of diffuse endometrial cancers, but misses localized focal polyps in forty percent of cases. When bleeding continues despite a negative biopsy, perform hysteroscopy.

steps.tx: **Hysteroscopy** with directed biopsy represents the definitive gold standard for direct visual inspection of the uterine cavity. Utilizing normal saline as an optical distension medium, a fine diagnostic hysteroscope visualizes the entire endocervical canal, uterine cavity, tubal ostia, and vascular patterns. Any focal polypoid projection, submucosal leiomyoma, or friable atypical vascular tufting is biopsied under direct vision using miniature grasp forceps, entirely eliminating the sampling errors inherent to blind aspiration techniques.
steps.say: Hysteroscopy directly visualizes the endometrial cavity using saline distension. It inspects every millimeter under magnification, allowing targeted biopsy of focal polyps and suspicious vessels that blind biopsies miss.

nodes.label: Hysteroscopic Biopsy
nodes.sub: Indicated if TVUS >4 mm, Pipelle fails, or bleeding recurs

steps.tx: **Endometrial hyperplasia** represents a spectrum of proliferative glandular alterations grouped by the World Health Organization into two distinct biological categories: hyperplasia without atypia and atypical hyperplasia (also designated endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia, EIN). Non-atypical hyperplasia reflects prolonged, unopposed estrogen stimulation with crowded, dilated glands that retain cytological polarity, carrying a progression risk to cancer under two percent. In contrast, atypical hyperplasia displays nuclear stratification, rounded vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli.
steps.say: Endometrial hyperplasia is divided into non-atypical and atypical types. Hyperplasia without atypia has under two percent cancer risk, while atypical hyperplasia carries a significant forty percent risk of harboring cancer.

vis.title: WHO Classification of Endometrial Hyperplasia
rows: Loss of nuclear polarity, enlarged pleomorphic nuclei

steps.tx: **Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system** (LNG-IUS 52 mg) provides the first-line medical therapy for endometrial hyperplasia without atypia. Delivering twenty micrograms of levonorgestrel daily directly into the uterine cavity, it induces profound glandular atrophy and extensive decidualization of the stroma, achieving regression rates exceeding ninety percent within six months. Oral progestogens such as medroxyprogesterone acetate ten milligrams daily or continuous micronized progesterone represent second-line alternatives, requiring surveillance biopsy every six months until two consecutive negative specimens are confirmed.
steps.say: The 52-milligram levonorgestrel intrauterine system is the first-line medical treatment for non-atypical hyperplasia, achieving over ninety percent regression. Re-biopsy every six months until two clear specimens are documented.

right.title: Atypical Hyperplasia / EIN
points: Mandated due to concurrent cancer hazard
High-dose progestins only if preserving fertility

steps.tx: **Total hysterectomy** with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy represents the definitive surgical standard of care for atypical hyperplasia and endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia. Because concurrent, undetected invasive endometrial adenocarcinoma is discovered in thirty to forty percent of hysterectomy specimens following a preoperative biopsy of atypical hyperplasia, medical therapy is inherently hazardous. Conservative high-dose progestogen therapy is reserved strictly for premenopausal women who strongly desire future childbearing, requiring mandatory endometrial surveillance biopsies every three months.
steps.say: Total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy is the standard treatment for atypical hyperplasia because up to forty percent of surgical specimens harbor coexisting adenocarcinoma that the biopsy missed.
